modelSocketShutdownJournal.coreTests: One staged empty-cache shutdown, journal and restored-quarantine case; five acquisition cases, one owner-identity case and one paired staging case passed

modelSocketCancellationEvidence.coreTests: Two interruption cases, one normal journal case, five acquisition cases and one owner identity case passed

cachedSocketLoopback.coreTests: Real cached socket loopback test, two controlled cancellation cases and normal staged journal regression passed

stagedRealSocketShutdown.coreTests: One staged real cached socket test, two controlled cancellation cases and five acquisition cases passed

realSocketCancellation.coreTests: Two real socket cancellation cases, one normal real socket journal case and two empty-cache cancellation regressions passed

modelSocketProcessDeath.coreTests: One parent process test covering two killed children, two controlled cancellation regressions and five acquisition cases passed

restoredDestinationCancellationVerificat.hostRegression: 227 native-control, journal and verifier transport checks passed.

After tightening saturation handling, a standalone Rust test extracted from the helper passed normal/intervening/saturation cases, and final app-server build and two broker cases (checkpoint and normal shutdown) passed. Patch forward/reverse and whitespace checks passed; the full Core suite was not rerun.
postShutdownContributorWitness.limitations: Point-in-time checks cannot prevent later or remote changes and do not establish destination authority; uncertain outcomes remain quarantined. Full Core and end-to-end Gate 2 acceptance remain open.

sourceModelDestinationWitness.scope: Experimental retained destination checks before and after source model shutdown and before live receipt observation; failures retain uncertainty.
sourceModelDestinationWitness.validation: The previous build demonstrably closed the source model socket after the destination memory changed. Current offline app-server build passed. Five broker/app-server cases passed across runs: real socket shutdown, lost reply recovery, memory drift before shutdown, during its effect, and before live receipt observation. The first run passed three and failed two because their assertions expected an exception instead of the protocol’s null observation; both passed after correcting assertions and checking the host journal remained uncertain. Patch forward/reverse and whitespace checks passed; full Core suite was not rerun.
sourceModelDestinationWitness.limitations: Checks observe retained local state at points in time and do not exclude later or remote changes, establish complete destination authority, or authorize receiver release.

postPublicationInstructionWitness.scope: Experimental retained destination instruction revalidation around source MCP and model shutdown, using existing native instruction preparation.
postPublicationInstructionWitness.validation: The preceding app-server build incorrectly allowed source shutdown after a real destination AGENTS.md change. postPublicationInstructionWitness.limitations: Revalidation reads the captured instruction scope at bounded points; it does not prevent later changes, verify all destination authority or remote work, or authorize receiver release.

postPublicationSkillPluginWitness.limitations: The retained plugin selection and skill input checks are local, bounded observations; they do not exclude subsequent changes or establish complete destination authority, remote work or receiver release.

resolvedStoreGuardVerification.scope: Opt-in point-in-time checks in native Config, StateRuntime and direct SqliteConfig pool opens. Managed sqlite_home and log paths must resolve to the expected existing store; app-server uses strict config while enabled. This does not verify Desktop process identity, protect prior opens, hold paths against replacement, protect SQLite sidecars or exclude external or same-UID writers. Direct SQLite access bypassing these entry points is not covered.
resolvedStoreGuardVerification.nativeIntegration: Isolated debug app-server passed an allowed-path control and refused configured sqlite_home, log_dir and debug-injected managed sqlite_home overrides before opening either SQLite store; strict fallback was exercised without --strict-config.
resolvedStoreGuardVerification.stateTests: Two focused codex-state tests passed, including direct StateRuntime refusal before directory creation, direct pool outside-path refusal and database symlink refusal.

mcpConstructionDiagnostic.scope: Static debug progress markers and fixed refusal stages without inputs or secrets; no safety decisions changed.
mcpConstructionDiagnostic.nativeIntegration: One earlier full VM case passed and another failed before XPC during MCP construction. A first instrumented run refused construction with owner valid. Four later runs with finer progress markers and the same rebuilt binary passed grant, XPC guest revocation, service crash and guest recovery. The intermittent refusal was not reproduced with fine markers and its cause remains unknown. A subsequent instrumented run failed after runtime publication and required-server validation, during cached binding observation; no grant was reached.

boundedMcpCatalogWait.scope: Experimental five-second bounded read-only wait for optional catalog stability, with owner liveness checks and existing native revalidation before at most one capture. No receiver release or production supervisor enabled.
boundedMcpCatalogWait.validation: Offline build and patch forward/reverse and whitespace checks passed. One integration with the final binary passed guest revocation, restart, new test adapter credential, quarantined native successor and observation of the same broker grant; source detached and MCP historically closed while remote work remains unresolved and receiver held. A debug-only simulated never-stable catalog refused after the bounded wait, retained uncertainty and quarantine, and invoked constructMcp once. JavaScript regressions passed 207/207.
boundedMcpCatalogWait.limitations: The earlier intermittent rejection was narrowed to binding capture. The bounded wait addresses a startup stability race but does not establish that all causes of binding refusal are resolved; the negative readiness condition is injected, not an actual failed server. Broker grant observation is not proof of remote completion, physical isolation, or authorization to dispatch or release.

experimentalMcpAttemptJournal.scope: Debug-only, opt-in, per-transport-attempt journal at the common native MCP send path. A scoped bounded 1024-slot directory is synced before sending. Records remain uncertain after local reply and are not a remote completion receipt. No production migration or receiver-release path uses this journal.
experimentalMcpAttemptJournal.validation: Offline build and patch forward/reverse and whitespace checks passed. Actual Codex app-server tests covered direct MCP RPC and a model-generated prepared binding call, crash after and during HTTP send with a retained uncertain record after restart, session-expiry 404 recovery with two separately recorded sends, and full-slot refusal with no remote send. A model-call cancellation preserved both uncertain records and the fixture cleanup completed after the cooperative lock stale interval. npm run check passed.
experimentalMcpAttemptJournal.limitations: Same-UID journal directory and scope are not an authenticated owner, server identity or complete global inventory; operations before enabling the fixture or outside these calls are not covered. No backend has supplied a verifiable terminal receipt. Local replies never close records. The first two cancellation attempts failed cleanup because fixture cleanup waited 10 seconds while its watchdog waits up to 75 seconds; they retained state and their stopped fixture containers were subsequently removed via their exact journals without breaking locks. No gate closure, remote completion, OS isolation or receiver release is established.

experimentalMcpOwnerFd.scope: Experimental debug-only inherited FD owner channel at the common MCP transport-attempt path. Exact grant digest and monotonically numbered requests are required; record and directory are synced before ACK. Channel failure refuses the call; local replies do not settle remote work.
experimentalMcpOwnerFd.validation: Offline cargo check and app-server build passed. A real app-server called a loopback MCP tool after a scoped record and refused another call after channel closure. Native SIGKILL after send retained an uncertain record visible to a successor without replay. A separate same-UID supervisor fixture spawned a real app-server after a real broker bound the grant; adapter revocation closed the lease and prevented a second remote send. Foreign scope rejection and owner recovery also passed. Reverse patch check passed for codex-rs paths; full reverse check was obstructed by existing .vscode files.
experimentalMcpOwnerFd.limitations: The supervisor launcher and broker share a UID and are fixtures, not a verified system supervisor or isolated account. No authenticated two-UID launch, complete process coverage, global remote inventory, backend completion receipt, atomic revocation against dispatch, receiver release or migration acceptance is established. Non-debug opt-in is refused.

experimentalPrivateJournalInspection.scope: Debug-only private observation of a durable imported grant-bound journal, without constructing a session or allowing release.
experimentalPrivateJournalInspection.validation: Offline native build and isolated checkpoint import test passed. Two concurrent inspections succeeded, a mismatched grant was refused, and the thread remained unloaded with no fixture-provider request. Public resume by ID or path was refused before loading a session, leaving the journal unchanged; an ordinary thread resumed normally. The host wrapper discarded a native observation after real broker adapter revocation before its second authorization. The codex-rs patch reverse check passed.
experimentalPrivateJournalInspection.limitations: This observes only a journal; it is not a native policy codec, effective configuration approval, broker revocation proof, hook isolation proof, OS identity or receiver release. The inherited private descriptor and same-UID review environment are not production trust boundaries.

experimentalNativeCheckpoint.scope: Debug-only native export of bounded rollout and durable continuity journal in chunks, tied to the exact live owner, reservation, approved grant and stable digest. A separate Linux review importer validates hashes, identities and the explicitly approved checkpointConfigSha256, then atomically publishes a fresh unverified home with rollout, journal and config. No release is authorized.
experimentalNativeCheckpoint.validation: Native cargo check and build passed. A real app-server and synthetic approved broker grant exported bounded chunks; SIGKILL before first chunk delivery kept the restarted thread quarantined. Linux review importer atomically published rollout, journal and separately approved config bytes, refused wrong or unapproved config and existing destinations, and reconciled a post-rename lost reply only as unverified. A managed SQLite-home override was refused by the native store guard before opening another store. Imported thread resume was explicitly refused for quarantine. The broker permits only checkpoint inspection and denies ordinary movement authorization and moved settlement. Selected source files reconstructed forward and the codex-rs patch reverse check passed.
experimentalNativeCheckpoint.limitations: The separately approved checkpointConfigSha256 binds file bytes only; effective native policy, managed overrides beyond the store guard, provider/auth/enforcer identity and cross-platform destination authority are not validated. The importer is a same-UID review fixture and assumes authenticated input and protected parent directory; no trusted two-UID launcher or full remote activity census is established. Guest app-server and vsock were tested separately against fixture authority; no imported session has run in the guest. No production migration or receiver release is enabled.

experimentalNativePolicyCandidate.scope: Unverified narrow native constraint recipes and anonymous provider candidate, plus shared SessionConfiguration assembly and experimental checkpoint metadata comparison. No broker second approval, complete policy view or execution authority is established.
experimentalNativePolicyCandidate.validation: Offline app-server build passed. Native Core tests passed for builder/metadata, bounded quota, local writer pin, environment invalidation and owner-close release while state is locked. With a real app-server and broker, a rollout mutation invalidated the observed snapshot and closed the private channel; adapter revocation closed the watched control and prevented revalidation. JavaScript native-control tests passed 140/140; codex-rs reverse patch check passed.
experimentalNativePolicyCandidate.limitations: Experimental same-UID fixture only. Local writer pin does not exclude other store instances or direct filesystem writers; the latter are detected on revalidation, not excluded. Native and broker watches do not make a cross-process database commit atomic with revocation. There is no durable export-digest binding, full effective policy, guest verifier or second approval. No production isolation or release is established.

pendingSharedCollaborationResolution.scope: Experimental private inspection reconstructs an anonymous quarantined candidate from receipt-digest-checked imported history, compares it with an independently reloaded native baseline, and retains it under the private owner with bounded time and quota. No policy approval or execution is authorized.
pendingSharedCollaborationResolution.validation: Rust sources parsed by rustfmt; codex-rs reverse patch check passed. JavaScript control tests pass. Changed Rust source and added native tests have not been compiled or run.
pendingSharedCollaborationResolution.limitations: The existing macOS app-server predates this change. Hashes alone do not authenticate a verifier; same-UID writes and revocation are not atomically excluded. Full policy projection, trusted guest verifier and second approval remain missing.
